headword: {暑中見舞|しょちゅうみま}い

definitions.explanation: A seasonal greeting card or message sent during the hottest part of summer (roughly mid-July to early August) to inquire after someone's well-being. One of several traditional seasonal greeting customs in Japan, along with New Year's cards.

examples.japanese: {暑中見舞|しょちゅうみま}いを{出|だ}した。
examples.english: I sent out summer greeting cards.

examples.japanese: {先生|せんせい}に{暑中見舞|しょちゅうみま}いのハガキを{書|か}いた。
examples.english: I wrote a summer greeting postcard to my teacher.

examples.japanese: {暑中見舞|しょちゅうみま}い{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます。
examples.english: I extend my midsummer greetings to you. (standard opening phrase)

examples.japanese: {立秋|りっしゅう}を{過|す}ぎたら{暑中見舞|しょちゅうみま}いではなく{残暑見舞|ざんしょみま}いになる。
examples.english: After the start of autumn on the traditional calendar, it becomes a late-summer greeting rather than a midsummer greeting.

notes:
Composed of {暑中|しょちゅう} (the heat of midsummer; the hottest period) and {見舞|みま}い (inquiry after someone's health; a visit or greeting of sympathy). Literally "midsummer health inquiry."

This is one of Japan's important seasonal correspondence customs. Cards are sent during the period called {暑中|しょちゅう}, roughly from mid-July until {立秋|りっしゅう} (start of autumn, around August 7). After {立秋|りっしゅう}, the same type of greeting shifts to {残暑見舞|ざんしょみま}い (late-summer greeting).

The standard opening phrase on these cards is {暑中|しょちゅう}お{見舞|みま}い{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます, a highly formal expression of seasonal well-wishing.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {暑中見舞|しょちゅうみま}いを{出|だ}す: to send summer greeting cards
- {暑中見舞|しょちゅうみま}いのハガキ: summer greeting postcard
- {暑中見舞|しょちゅうみま}い{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます: standard summer greeting phrase

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {年賀状|ねんがじょう}: New Year's card — the other major seasonal greeting card tradition
- {残暑見舞|ざんしょみま}い: late-summer greeting — sent after {立秋|りっしゅう}, when the summer heat lingers
- {寒中見舞|かんちゅうみま}い: midwinter greeting — the winter equivalent
